root_cause.text: The `emac_tx_mem_map()` function failed to free previously allocated DMA mappings when a mapping error occurred during packet transmission, causing a resource leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds cleanup code in the `err_free_skb` error handling path that iterates through all allocated transmit buffer descriptors (from `old_head` to `head`) and calls `emac_free_tx_buf(priv, i)` to properly deallocate the DMA mappings. Before this fix, the error path only called `dev_kfree_skb_any(skb)` without freeing the DMA resources that had already been mapped, as indicated by the commit message stating "The DMA mappings were leaked on mapping error."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix TX descriptor memory leak in error path by properly freeing allocated TX buffers before skb deallocation.
intent_record.what: Added a loop in the error handling path (err_free_skb label) that iterates from old_head to head, calling emac_free_tx_buf() for each descriptor index with wraparound handling, before the existing dev_kfree_skb_any() call.
intent_record.how: When an error occurs during TX memory mapping, the code now properly cleans up any TX buffer descriptors that were allocated between old_head and head before freeing the skb. Previously, these descriptors were leaked. The loop correctly handles ring wraparound by resetting the index to 0 when it reaches tx_ring->total_cnt.

bic_trace_step.reason: The `emac_tx_mem_map()` function (lines 1047-1107) contains the vulnerable construct. When `emac_tx_map_frag()` fails at line 1089 with a DMA mapping error, the function jumps to `err_free_skb` label (line 1105) which only calls `dev_kfree_skb_any(skb)` and `dev_dstats_tx_dropped()`. However, it does NOT call `emac_free_tx_buf()` to unmap the previously allocated DMA mappings from earlier iterations of the loop (lines 1078-1104). The loop processes fragments incrementally, and if a mapping error occurs on fragment `f`, all successfully mapped fragments from `f=0` to `f-1` have their DMA addresses stored in `tx_buf->buf[buf_idx].dma_addr` but are never unmapped. This causes a resource leak of DMA mappings. The fix would require calling `emac_free_tx_buf(priv, old_head)` or similar cleanup logic before jumping to the error handler to properly unmap all previously allocated DMA resources.
